memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "You, however, will go to your ancestors in peace and be buried at a good old age. In the fourth generation your descendants will come back here, for the sin of the Amorites has not yet reached its full measure." - Gen 15:15-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God tells Abram something quietly beautiful: "You will go to your ancestors in peace and be buried at a good old age." Abram would not live to see the promise fulfilled. He would die with the land still occupied and his descendants still few. And yet - he would die in peace.

That is a profound gift. Peace does not require seeing the outcome. Abram could go to his grave content, not because everything was resolved, but because he trusted the One who promised. Faith can die peacefully with the story unfinished.

Then comes a striking line: "the sin of the Amorites has not yet reached its full measure." God delays four hundred years - not out of indifference, but out of patience. He was giving the Amorites centuries to turn back before judgement came. What looked like delay was actually mercy toward a people who weren't even Abram's concern.

God's timing is never arbitrary. Behind every delay is a purpose we often cannot see - frequently mercy toward someone else. "The Lord is not slow in keeping his promise... he is patient with you, not wanting anyone to perish" (2 Pet 3:9). You may not see the fulfilment in your lifetime. You can still go in peace.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Could you be at peace even if you never see the outcome you're praying for?
- Might God's delay in your life be mercy toward someone else?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, give me peace that doesn't depend on seeing the outcome. Help me trust Your timing, knowing Your delays are full of purpose and mercy. Let me rest in Your faithfulness, whatever I live to see.
Amen.
